'''Ronald Edmund Dupree Jr.''' (born January 26, 1981) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played six seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He also played numerous seasons in the [[NBA Development League]], and spent time in Europe and Argentina. After his playing retirement, Dupree was a college basketball assistant coach and works as a scout for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].

==College career==
Dupree played at [[Louisiana State University]] (LSU) under [[John Brady (basketball)|Coach John Brady]]. He averaged 4.9 points and 3.3 rebounds in 12.7 minutes per game in the Tigers' 2000 Sweet Sixteen season. He was named All-SEC Second Team in his sophomore, junior, and senior seasons. During his sophomore season he led the SEC in scoring at 17.3 points per game and was second in rebounding with 8.8 per game.  In each of his last three years he ranked second in the SEC in rebounding with averages of 8.8 (2000–2001), 8.5 (2001–2002), and 8.3 (2002–2003). He also never finished lower than seventh in the league in scoring in his final three seasons.  He finished his LSU career as the school's eighth-most-prolific scorer and sixth-best rebounder.

==Professional career==
Dupree went undrafted in 2003, but signed during the [[2003–04 NBA season|2003–04 season]] with the [[Chicago Bulls]]. After his rookie season, he signed a contract with the [[Detroit Pistons]], but was infrequently used by coach [[Larry Brown (basketball)|Larry Brown]]. Dupree was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] prior to the 2005–06 season for a second-round draft pick. He re-signed with the Pistons on July 17, 2006.  On December 14, 2007, he was waived so the Pistons could make room for other players obtained in a trade with the [[Charlotte Bobcats]]. He was signed to a ten-day contract by the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] on April 3, 2008, becoming the last player to sign with the Sonics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.seattlepi.com/news/article/Sonics-Notebook-Sonics-sign-Dupree-to-10-day-deal-1269221.php|title=Sonics Notebook: Sonics sign Dupree to 10-day deal|last=Washburn|first=Gary|last2=Reporter|first2=P.-I.|date=2008-04-04|website=seattlepi.com|access-date=2019-05-19}}</ref>

Dupree started the 2008–2009 season with the [[Tulsa 66ers]] of the NBA Developmental League. Halfway through the season he was traded to the [[Utah Flash]], and helped take that team to the D-League finals. Dupree was invited to training camp with the [[Utah Jazz]] for preparation to the 2009–2010 season. However, he did not make their final roster.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/62282/20091022/jazz_waive_dupree_harris/ |title=Jazz Waive Dupree, Harris |access-date=October 22, 2009 |archive-date=October 24, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091024222203/http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/62282/20091022/jazz_waive_dupree_harris |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He signed a non-guaranteed contract with the [[Toronto Raptors]] on September 16, 2010. Dupree was released from the Toronto Raptors roster on October 19, 2010. He was re-signed by Toronto on December 26, 2010,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/20101226/7829/raptors-re-sign-dupree|title=Raptors Re-Sign Dupree|website=Toronto Raptors|language=en|access-date=2019-05-19}}</ref> but waived again on January 5, 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/70967/20110105/raptors_waive_ronald_dupree/ |title=Raptors Waive Ronald Dupree |access-date=January 6, 2011 |archive-date=January 7, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110107090025/http://www.realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/70967/20110105/raptors_waive_ronald_dupree/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He signed with the Argentine team [[Regatas Corrientes]] in January 2012. He then signed with the Italian team Andrea Costa Imola Basket in February 2012. In September 2012, he joined the [[Memphis Grizzlies]],<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11017 Memphis Grizzlies add Michael Dunigan, Ronald Dupree, Jarrid Famous, Jerome Jordan, D.J. Kennedy to training camp]</ref> but he did not make the team's regular season roster.<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11315 Memphis Grizzlies waive Ronald Dupree, Jerome Jordan, Ronald Murray]</ref>

On January 4, 2013, Dupree was acquired by the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/130104_dupree.html D-Fenders Acquire Ronald Dupree]</ref> On February 25, 2013, Dupree was traded to the [[Reno Bighorns]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/130225_jordan.html D-Fenders Trade for Jerome Jordan] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130227042006/http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/130225_jordan.html |date=2013-02-27 }}</ref> On August 8, 2013, he signed a two-year deal with [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]].<ref>{{cite web|title=HAPOEL JERUSALEM picks up Dupree|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2013-14/i/115319/8174|publisher=Eurocupbasketball.com|accessdate=9 August 2013|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130811161314/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2013-14/i/115319/8174|archivedate=11 August 2013}}</ref>

On September 10, 2014, he announced his retirement and became a student assistant on the LSU men's basketball staff.<ref>{{cite web|title=LSU basketball hires former player Ronald Dupree as student assistant|url=http://www.lsureveille.com/daily/lsu-basketball-hires-former-player-ronald-dupree-as-student-assistant/article_b5948da6-37a5-11e4-a277-0017a43b2370.html}}</ref>

== Post-playing career==
Dupree returned to LSU as a student assistant coach in 2014.<ref>{{cite web |title=Former LSU standout Ronald Dupree will spend 2014-15 season as a student assistant coach |url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/former-lsu-standout-ronald-dupree-will-spend-2014-15-season-as-a-student-assistant-coach/article_200a511b-b4fe-5c1b-90a6-9d7a24f835e5.html |website=The Advocate |access-date=June 27, 2024 |date=September 9, 2014}}</ref> He was elevated to the position of director of student development for the 2015–16 season.<ref name=murray>{{cite web |last1=Murray |first1=Chris |title=Wolf Pack assistant Ronald Dupree leaves for NBA job |url=https://www.rgj.com/story/sports/college/nevada/2017/07/26/wolf-pack-assistant-ronald-dupree-leaves-nba-job/514573001/ |website=Reno Gazette Journal |access-date=June 27, 2024 |date=July 27, 2017}}</ref> Dupree was hired by the [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball team]] as an assistant coach for the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Coach Muss talks assistant coach Ronald Dupree |url=https://nevadawolfpack.com/news/2016/11/5/Coach_Muss_talks_assistant_coach_Ronald_Dupree.aspx |website=Nevada Wolf Pack |access-date=June 27, 2024 |date=November 5, 2016}}</ref> He departed the position in 2017 to join the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] as a scout.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bucks expand staff, name ex-Wolves GM Milt Newton assistant general manager |url=https://onmilwaukee.com/articles/bucks-name-milt-newton-assistant-gm |website=On Milwaukee |access-date=June 27, 2024 |date=August 9, 2017}}</ref> In 2025, Dupree returned to LSU again to take the newly created position of Basketball General Manager.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-07 |title=LSU taps Bucks exec Dupree for new GM job |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/44577520/lsu-taps-bucks-scouting-director-ronald-dupree-gm-job |access-date=2025-12-17 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>
